# Instructions for accurately documenting company losses in a financial disclosure

1. Start with the accounting records.
2.
completion:
Make a note of how the numbers are derived
3. Adjust for changes in GAAP, and provide a reconciliation.
4. Adjust for different currencies.
5. Use the same method consistently every quarter.
6. Exclude charges and credits not related to operations.
7. Select a time period with no internal problems.
8. Don’t adjust gross margins or similar measures.
9. Don’t adjust for changes in markets or competitors, or for “structural competitive differences”.
10. Don’t make big upward adjustments for acquisitions.
11. Don’t explain changes in a segment if they are not used to measure a management performance.
12. Don’t assume that everybody knows what a restatement is.
13. Don’t focus on per-share numbers.
14. Don’t put out a loss press release right before earnings.
